pull.title: guix: declare python-setuptools in codesign manifest
pull.body:
Since we bumped to python 3.12, `setuptools` is no longer provided by default: https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html#ensurepip Declare this explicitly.

Also bypass `certvalidator`'s custom test loader using `unittest`, until [this upstream patch](https://github.com/LRGH/elfesteem/commit/000d6bbcd3a4b3d132ad6d932eedb3158b3313e9)  makes it into our Guix time machine commit.

Commits split to allow easy reversion of only the `imp` test loader patch.

Fixes: #36421

guix: declare python-setuptools

Since we bumpted to python 3.12, setuptools is no longer provided by
default:

https://docs.python.org/3.12/whatsnew/3.12.html#ensurepip

> easy_install, pkg_resources, setuptools and distutils are no longer
> provided by default in environments created with venv or bootstrapped
> with ensurepip, since they are part of the setuptools package. For
> projects relying on these at runtime, the setuptools project should be
> declared as a dependency and installed separately (typically, using
> pip).

committer will <will@256k1.dev> 1791280392 +0100

guix: update certvalidator for Python 3.12

Python 3.12 removed imp, breaking the pinned Certvalidator test loader.

achow101 rebased allow-more-criticals onto upstream, which includes the
loader fix.

However the runner preloads oscrypto's OpenSSL backend, whose discovered
library names cannot be resolved in the isolated Guix build. Set its
supported OSCRYPTO_USE_OPENSSL variable to absolute library paths from
the existing OpenSSL input so the test suite can run.

events.body:
Thanks @achow101

I have pushed a new second commit here, but unfortunately that rebase was not totally issue-free on its own :(

https://github.com/wbond/certvalidator/commit/9618d1b03564c9e09af13036146522112bb6006e introduces an early import of oscrypto's OpenSSL backend to print the library version before running tests. This fails in the Guix container because the dynamic loader cannot resolve `libcrypto.so.3`.

I've therefore set `OSCRYPTO_USE_OPENSSL` to the absolute library paths from our existing OpenSSL input.

If anyone has a better approach, I'm all ears :)
